items.summary: The 10-30 anti-heal coverage plan gets trimmed: one Healbane is unchanged, but a second source adds less and a fourth caps at 72% instead of 82%. That is a soft buff to dedicated healers and a soft nerf to teams stacking Healbane as a team slot.

affected_heroes.why: His Healbane is the team's anti-sustain coverage; the lower 4-stack cap reduces the payoff when allies also buy it.
Healbane plus Toxic Bullets was his anti-heal package into healer comps; harsher multi-source diminishing returns trims that combo.
His built-in heal cut plus Healbane/Toxic Bullets was a real anti-sustain answer; the stacking nerf weakens that composition.
Healbane is a bruiser-sustain cut in her on-hit core; it loses value mainly when the team stacks anti-heal.
Healbane is a sustain/anti-heal slot in his spirit-amp core; single-source use is unchanged.
He buys Healbane in the utility build, but as a Locket/heal-sustain hero he benefits more from enemy anti-heal stacking being weaker.
Dome/regen sustain is his win condition; weaker stacked anti-heal lets his heals survive coordinated Healbane buys.
Tether healing was the main casualty of 10-30 anti-heal stacking; this patch gives it some relief.
Scorn sustain gets more value when enemy anti-heal caps lower; his own Healbane is secondary.
His regen/sustain shell was taxed by stacked anti-heal; the lower 4-stack cap helps him start fights healthier.

items.build_shift: No component or slot change: Healbane remains a Vitality T2. The shift is strategic — one Healbane is still the same, but a second or third buyer now adds less, so teams should stop treating it as a coverage slot and let one dedicated buyer hold it.

notable_item_stories: Healbane is the patch's only item move, so the item meta is otherwise frozen; the change mainly rebalances sustain comps against anti-heal comps.
Expect fewer double-Healbane buys in coordinated play: one dedicated buyer is enough, and over-stacking anti-heal is now less efficient.
